messages:
maria: Quick ask — we need a crisp go/no-go checklist for GA tomorrow. Top-level items: SLA targets, docs, support rota, monitoring, pricing/cost guardrails. Can owners confirm items and where they're documented? (cc @akshay @liz @sam) :eyes:
akshay: SLA proposal: 99.9% availability + latency buckets per model class. I'll post numbers in a sec. Also need clarity on support windows (24/7 vs biz hours) per tier.
liz: Monitoring baseline: alerts we want by GA: model crash rate >1% over 5m, P99 latency spikes (relative to baseline) sustained for 5m, container OOMs, and Kafka backpressure. I have a runbook but want to confirm escalation path — auto-fallback to compatible variant or pager to eng-oncall?
sam: Docs checklist: 1) public SLA page 2) internal ops runbook 3) support playbook (escalation ladder) 4) troubleshooting FAQ. I can draft wording for SLA and ops summary once numbers are final. Where should the public page live? Redwood Docs main site and an internal confluence for runbooks.
jordan: Support constraints: GA requires 24/7 oncall coverage only for Enterprise customers. Self-serve gets business-hours live support + async SLA (response within 24h). Need a clear escalation list (pager -> eng oncall -> senior eng) and training for CS/triage. Who owns training?
maria: Action owners: Akshay (SLA numbers + rollout policy), Liz (runbook + monitoring alerts), Sam (SLA wording + public docs draft), Jordan (support tiers doc + training). I'll own commercial messaging and pricing guardrails.
akshay: Proposed latency/availability numbers (initial): Hosted API (standard): availability 99.9% monthly; text-gen small models p50 < 80ms, p95 < 300ms. Large models p50 < 200ms, p95 < 800ms. Dedicated pools: availability 99.95% and prioritized scheduling; embeddings: p95 < 100ms. These are provisional — open to tweaks.
liz: Runbook link (draft): https://internal.redwood/runbooks/ga-sla — contains playbooks: fallback to compatible variant, clear circuit-breaker thresholds, KV cache invalidation steps. Alerts: send pager to eng-oncall if crash rate >0.5% sustained for 10m. Also recommend automated model-swap to a lower-cost variant on high-error events.
sam: Draft SLA snippet for legal review: "We strive to provide 99.9% monthly availability for the Hosted API. If availability for a given calendar month falls below 99.9%, customers may be eligible for service credits. Credits and thresholds to be defined in the final contract." I'll draft the credit table and push to docs branch later today. Need legal signoff on exclusions (abuse, customer misconfig, force majeure).
maria: Pricing guardrails: we need a hard budget cap for self-serve burst to prevent runaway bills — suggest daily budget cap and email + hard stop after threshold. FinOps to set default X/day; commercial can increase per customer. Also define overage behavior (auto-throttle vs bill). @finops please advise.
akshay: Canary/rollout plan: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated quality checks (error rate, latency, quality regression via eval set). If any threshold breached, auto-rollback. We need console defaults for those thresholds and an operator-visible rollout timeline. I can wire automation for rollback and metrics hooks.
liz: Gap: we don't have per-customer SLO dashboards for private deployments — that blocks offering Enterprise SLA for private installs. Proposal: require dedicated metrics ingestion or ship an agent that forwards key metrics. Adding this as a non-optional checklist item for Private.
jordan: Ops training: I'll run a 1-hour session tomorrow 10:00 UTC for oncall + support. Sam can you prepare a 5-slide summary + runbook highlights? Need contact list (phone + pager) for escalation and a simple RACI for who does what during incidents.
sam: Will have SLA page + ops summary by EOD. Draft pushed to docs branch: https://docs.redwood/sla/ga-draft — feedback welcome.
maria: Legal items: need standard exclusions (force majeure, maintenance windows), and explicit non-applicability for misuse/abuse. Also confirm maintenance notification windows and scheduled maintenance SLA carve-outs. @legal-bot please review when ready.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: canary start 2024-10-03T02:00Z. Rolling window 4h. Watch alerts and rollback policy enabled.
liz: Small ask — increase tracing retention to 30d for GA to aid post-incident debugging. That will increase infra costs; flagging for FinOps.
maria: Decisions from this thread: 1) Accept Akshay's latency targets as provisional. 2) 24/7 oncall required for Enterprise customers; self-serve gets business-hours + async SLA. 3) Sam to deliver public SLA and ops summary by EOD. 4) Jordan to run ops training tomorrow. 5) Legal to sign off SLA early tomorrow. Action owners assigned above. :thumbsup: 
jordan: I'll assemble a RACI and post into #product after the training. Also will add escalation contact list.
sam: Noted — ping me for any phrasing tweaks from legal.
akshay: I'll implement the rollout automation and default thresholds in the console and ensure metrics hooks for rollback.
liz: I'll augment the Enterprise checklist with the private-deploy metrics requirement and add the 30d tracing retention request.
maria: Thanks everyone. If there are no objections by 14:00 UTC we'll consider this the working go-ahead for GA prep. :rocket:
